items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: He and Tony Jackson around Chicago during that period. I was about, see, 21, 22, 23, I was around. I was about 12, 13 years old.

ctx.x: Excuse me Danny, what was the name of the band you were with then?

I was with Lee Collins, Jones and Collins. Astoria Band. We played at Astoria. We played in New Orleans on Rampart Street which was owned by Beansy Furrier. It had once been owned by, I can't think of a man's name. It was a brewery people. Beansy took it over. It was a gambling concession. and we worked there. And Professor Cook was the emcee in musical and performance director and everything. He was the wheel around there. So he staged this train excursion to Chicago, and we had our band to play. I had been to…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And there was another club where Tony Jackson was... I was looking at Ollie Powers and Tony Jackson in another club.

ctx.x: Why did you first go to Chicago in 1921?

My uncle Paul Barbarin was with King Oliver. He sent for his mother to come up. She said, “I’ll take Willie.” That’s my uncle. He’s two years older than me. I’m what? 10. Willie’s 12. So I started crying, “I want to go.” So they talked about it. Said all right. You take me too, so there’s two of us. My grandmother and my grandfather and me [? (inaudible)] and Willie, my uncle, we go to Chicago. Paul. I’m there. I’m hearing music all the time, because Chicago’s a all-night town. Speakeasy town. Me and Willie would…
[? (inaudible)], laying on our stomach. You see the men kissing the women, feeling on the women. You see the band playing. I was looking at Ollie Powers and Tony Jackson in another club.
